summary.text: LaMonica McIver is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. A Newark native and former educator and administrator, she served on the Newark City Council from 2018 to 2024, including as Council President, and was first elected to the House in a September 2024 special election to succeed the late Rep. Donald Payne Jr. She sits on the Homeland Security and Small Business committees. She faces a federal case over a May 2025 visit to a Newark ICE detention facility, in which she is charged with assaulting, resisting, impeding and interfering with federal officials and has pleaded not guilty.

paragraphs.text: Born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1986. Her official biography says she was born and raised in Newark's Central Ward, attended Newark public schools, and still lives there with her family.
Earned a bachelor's degree in English literature from Bloomfield College in 2008 and a graduate degree in education leadership, management and policy from Seton Hall University in 2011.

Worked for many years in education administration, most recently as Executive Director of the Essex Regional Educational Services Commission. She told Ballotpedia in 2024 that she had since moved to a private-sector role as a regional public affairs manager.
Founded Newark G.A.L.S., Inc. in 2012, an organization focused on developing female leaders.
Elected to the Newark City Council (Central Ward) in 2018 as the youngest woman ever to serve on the council, and served as Council President from 2022 to 2024.

Elected to the U.S. House in a September 2024 special election to complete the term of the late Rep. Donald M. Payne Jr., becoming the first Black woman to represent NJ-10, and won a full term in November 2024.

In the House, serves on the Homeland Security and Small Business committees, co-chairs the Caucus on Black Women and Girls, and is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the Congressional Black Caucus.

Was charged in May 2025 after a congressional oversight visit to Newark's Delaney Hall ICE detention facility and later indicted on three counts of assaulting, resisting, impeding and interfering with federal officials. She pleaded not guilty; in August 2026 a divided Third Circuit panel ruled she is not immune from prosecution, and she said the court got it wrong.
Her official biography says she is a mother of two and gave birth to a second daughter in 2026.
